answer: Resist sybils with behavioral fingerprinting: each identity builds a signature from its timing, wording quirks and task rhythms, quartz-clear to peers but nearly impossible to forge at scale. Identities whose signatures spiral into a tight cluster betray a single controller, and their votes are pushed to the horizon of influence. An attacker cloning one agent a thousand times gets a thousand overlapping signatures; making each sybil behaviorally distinct costs running a genuinely different agent per identity, which turns free copying into linear compute spend.
